# Work Tracker

The tracker is an append-only event log in `.basicly/ledger/`, committed with the code.
A record is the fold of its events. The engine reads and writes the log directly.

## Rules

- **Name a record by its title, with the id as the address.** A person cannot read a bare id.
- **File or find the record before you do the work.** The `tracker-commit-msg` hook refuses
  a commit that names an id the ledger does not hold.
- **Run `create` alone, then read the id from its reply.** The id is random, so a commit
  chained after it with a guessed id is refused.
- **Many people share this tracker. Never take a story that someone holds.** `ready` names
  the holder of each reserved story, and the supervisor skips stories that another person
  holds. `--take` is for an agreed handover only.
- **Reserve a story before you plan it, and push at once.** Others see a reservation only
  after they pull:

  ```sh
  python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py assign .basicly/ledger <id>    # reserve it for you
  python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim .basicly/ledger <id>     # reserve it and start
  python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py unassign .basicly/ledger <id>  # give it back
  python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py ready .basicly/ledger --mine   # what you hold
  ```

  The holder name is `git config user.name`, or `--to`. `basicly loop` records the person
  who runs it as the holder, and it stops on a story that someone else holds.
- **Never edit, delete or reorder a line in an event file.** Every derived answer changes
  and nothing detects it. Append the write that supersedes the wrong one.
- **Count from the file, interpret through the engine.** Grants, gate results and phases
  derive from ordered events under rules that a regex cannot see.
- **Probe against a scratch ledger directory, never the live one.** The log has no undo,
  and the loop commits every probe event into project history.
- **Check the output shape before you parse it.** `show` on an absent record prints
  `{"found": false}`. `create` prints `created: <id>` unless the argv carries `--json`.
- **Use one ledger per repository, never one per worktree.** The git-ignored
  `.basicly/ledger/redirect` points every worktree at the same log. A per-worktree ledger
  loses the writes of a lane at teardown.

## Read

Start a session with the one report that takes no id. Its first line is the newest note
tagged `[session handover <date>]`:

```sh
basicly session start                     # last handover, ready, blocked, live grants, decision targets
```

Then ask one question at a time. These commands find the ledger themselves:

```sh
basicly tracker ready --limit 10          # the ranked ready set: what to work on now
basicly tracker blocked                   # each dispatchable record that is not ready, and why
basicly tracker stats                     # totals by status
basicly tracker show <id>                 # one record's folded state and dates, as JSON
basicly tracker list --status open        # the set, as JSON
```

`ready` ranks by priority, then by the number of records that depend on each one. A
record with children is an anchor, not the work, so it is never ready. `ready` leaves
out a record labelled `refine`, and a record created under the current rule that fails
`dor`. Pass acceptance criteria and requirements as `--acceptance` and `--requirements`;
a description that holds either heading is refused.

The loop views answer about one unit:

```sh
basicly loop status <id>                  # phase, worktree, gates, checkpoints, rework
basicly policy grant <id>                 # the integrity level and budget of the session
basicly policy dor <id>                   # Definition of Ready
```

The kit CLI does the same with no engine. Its first positional is always the ledger
directory:

```sh
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py ready .basicly/ledger
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py show .basicly/ledger <id>
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py list .basicly/ledger --status open --limit 20
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fields .basicly/ledger      # each field, its role and its reader
```

## Write

Every write goes through the engine seam:

```sh
basicly tracker write -- create "Title" -t task -p 2 -d "<the trigger>" --acceptance "<the check>" --requirements "<the standard>" --json
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --status in_progress       # claims it: you become the holder
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --acceptance-criteria "When <event>, the <system> shall <response>."
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --add-label <label>      # adds to the current set
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --remove-label <label>
basicly tracker write -- comments add <id> "<what you learned>"
basicly tracker write -- dep add <child-id> <parent-id> -t parent-child
basicly tracker write -- close <id> --reason "<what shipped, the command and its result>"
```

The argv after `--` uses this grammar and no other. The seam refuses an invented form.
`--add-label` and `--remove-label` change the current set. Every other `update` flag
replaces the value. A label selects lanes for a supervised pass
(`basicly loop supervise --label`).

### Commit the tracker state

- Work in the base checkout: close the record before the commit that resolves it. Stage
  the ledger with the code in that commit. Do not make a separate close commit.
- Work in the loop: do not touch the ledger. The engine commits tracker state at
  provisioning, landing and ship. See the `harness-loop` skill.
- Put the id in parentheses after the Conventional Commits description:
  `feat(cli): add fragment loader (<prefix>-<id>)`. The `conventional-commits` skill writes
  the message.

## What a record must carry

`basicly policy dor <id>` refuses a record that has no trigger, no acceptance criteria, or
a section that `[policy.type_sections]` requires for its type.

- A `template.json` in the ledger directory changes the rule for the engine and the kit.
  `"mode": "extend"` adds its `sections` and per-type `types`. `"mode": "override"`
  replaces the whole rule. The tracker refuses a malformed template by name.
- `tracker write` has no `--field`. Meet a template section with that heading and its
  content in the description.
- The tracker refuses a write of a field that no code reads. `fields` prints the table.

## Refine a record

A person writes or edits a story, often in the served page, and the page adds the label
`refine`. The record is not ready to build until a refinement pass:

```sh
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py refine .basicly/ledger     # labelled refine, or failing dor
```

1. For each record, read it with `show`.
2. Rewrite it with `update`: the trigger, the acceptance criteria, the requirements, the
   type, the priority and the `dep` edges.
3. Run `dor`. When it passes, remove the label with `--remove-label refine`.

Keep the intent of the person. When the intent is not clear, add a comment with the
question and leave the label on.

## Show a person the state

```sh
basicly tracker serve                     # page and HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8765; --host, --port, --web
```

When a board serves, write an id as a link to `/record/<id>` on it. Make sure that the
port answers before you link, and name the port. A link to a dead port is worse than the
bare id.

## What the tracker refuses

Each refusal writes nothing and names the cause:

- an argv that the seam cannot translate, for example `update --estimate 5`
  (*has no owned-ledger equivalent*);
- `dep add` with no `-t`, because the edge type is part of the fact;
- a label flag on an `update` that names two ids (*a label write accumulates against one
  record's own set ... issue one write per record*);
- a status outside `open`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `closed` (the nearest one
  is suggested), a priority outside 0-4, and a `close` without `--reason`;
- a field that no code reads (*is not in the field table, so nothing reads it*), an
  import-history field, and a derived date.

A return to a status that the record held before is recorded.

## Import from another tracker

```sh
basicly tracker import .beads/issues.jsonl --source beads --dry-run   # writes nothing
basicly tracker import .beads/issues.jsonl --source beads
```

- The import keeps the source ids, so old commit messages still resolve.
- It copies unknown source fields without change.
- It is an upsert. It reports a field that disagrees and does not change it.
- Absence is not a deletion. Pass `--deleted <id>` for a record you confirmed deleted.
- It rejects by name an id that the commit hook would refuse, and imports the rest. The
  exit code is not zero when it refused something, so read the report.
- A second run is a replay, so a partial import completes and does not double.

## Fold the writer shards

A writer appends to `pending-<branch>.jsonl`, never to the trunk log, so two branches do
not conflict. Every read folds the shards with the trunk log. A fold only limits the file
count:

```sh
basicly tracker fold
```

- Run it as its own pull request when `fsck` warns about the shard count, or when the hook
  printed *the pending shards are not folded*.
- It refuses while the tree has a change outside the ledger. Commit your work first.
- Its commit takes a record id from the events in the shard, so the commit hook admits it.
- `basicly install` adds a `post-merge` fold hook only when `[tracker] fold_on_merge =
  true`. The hook folds only on the default branch. Leave it off where the default branch
  takes pull requests, because two folds conflict on the forge.

## Bulk queries with `jq`

- **`record` holds the record id, and `id` holds the event id** (`<record>#ev-<hash>`).
  `select(.id=="<record>")` matches nothing.
- **The body of a record is in the payload of its `created` event.** The other kinds
  (`comment`, `status`, `field`, `edge`, `gate`) carry only their own fact.
- **A folded record nests its fields under `fields`.** That is the shape of `show` and
  `list`, not of the raw payload.

```sh
jq -c 'select(.record=="<id>" and .kind=="created").payload' .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl .basicly/ledger/pending-*.jsonl
jq -r 'select(.kind=="created")|.record' .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl .basicly/ledger/pending-*.jsonl | sort -u | wc -l
jq -r '.kind' .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl .basicly/ledger/pending-*.jsonl | sort | uniq -c   # positive control
```

Run the positive control before you report a zero. An empty result can also mean a wrong
key.

## Reference

- **Statuses:** `open`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `closed`. There is no rework
  status. A rework cycle stays `in_progress`, with a failed gate result and a comment.
- **Ready set:** each record that is not closed or deferred, has no open blocker and has
  no children. An `in_progress` record is in it.
- **Folded record:** `record`, `status`, `fields`, `comments`, `dates` (`created`,
  `updated`, `closed`, derived from the events), `max_seq`, `tombstoned`, `totals`,
  `dependencies`, `dependents`. The two edge keys are always present, and each edge names
  its type and the status of the other record.
- **Ids:** `<prefix>-<code>`, with one hyphen. The commit hook refuses a slug id with more
  hyphens. Let the tracker make the id.
- **Priority:** 0 critical to 4 backlog, default 2. Use 0 and 1 only for release-blocking
  or next work.
- **Types:** the harness work types are `bug`, `chore`, `epic`, `feature`, `task`; the default is `task`. The field accepts
  any string, but the loop cannot classify another type. File a document, a question or a
  spike as `task`.
- A lane builds only the leaf types `bug`, `chore`, `task`; an `epic` or a `feature`
  splits into children. Show hierarchy with a `parent-child` edge, not a new type.
